files.summary: Entry point for the spec set. It contains an index of all 28 planned spec files (path, title, owner, reviewer, phase, status), checked against the existing headers, with 6 files still marked Planned. It also covers: a reading guide; source precedence (spec PDF > C1–C18 > the spec that owns the topic > other specs > research inputs in critic > coherence > examiner > strategy order); a status legend (Planned/Draft/Review/Accepted/Frozen/Superseded); conventions (spec IDs vs registered Plotinium IDs, RFC 2119 marking, test naming, pilot-figure labels, errnos, Mermaid); and the change process. Before the stack freeze a change is a PR. After it, a normative change needs a docs/adr record plus the instructor's written approval (§14.4); editorial changes need only a labelled PR; after the W16 feature freeze only fix: PRs are merged. The README maps specs to code paths and to the 13 root documents of §15.1/§15.2, gives one-line summaries of C1–C18, and defines tests SPX-01..09.

Resumed and corrected, not restarted. Kept: plutonium origin framed as the element (density, energy, six allotropes), pronunciation, the weapons and hazard wording ban, the Plotinus risk and the viva answer, wordmark rules, the SVG logo brief (geometry re-checked), semver and gate tags, lattice-based codenames with isotope numbering rejected, exact uname -a format and /system/release format (spec p16), the §5.3 checklist, the token pointer, and the Appendix D form. Fixed: the header now has a Title row and the 2026-09-24 date. The alternative name Kernium was replaced by Tabium, because a web search found Kernium S.A. is an existing company; Orbitium, Lattium, Tessium, Ravium and Nimbium were also rejected, with cited sources. All 5 taglines now name all three differentiators, with computed character counts (74–89). The identity lint no longer flags 'atomic' in the ACID sense. Wording rules were added for the form's origin line. The ABNF now defines UTF8-nonascii. The cross-spec section records the requests other specs have accepted (PVFS-09, PVFS-02, UnameInfo, DSN-11, build identity in /api/readyz, shell uname) and those still open.

The master checklist. All 84 spec IDs are covered (77 Must, 5 Should, 2 May), each with keyword, summary, spec § and page, our spec, owner/reviewer, first gate, test titles and evidence. Test titles are copied verbatim from the owning specs where they exist; 23 are marked (proposed) where no spec has one yet. Evidence CI codes are derived from the test levels. Further sections: per-gate lists (G0..P5); the §10.1 structures mapped to 08-dsa's S1–S12 and DSA-* IDs; §15.2 documents (PLT-DOC-01..14); §13.1 phase deliverables; all 31 Appendix A lines with the live command, gate, owner and evidence; SYS-02 command owners aligned with the shell spec; §17.1 Demo Day and §17.2 deliverables (PLT-DEL-01..16); the team contract (PLT-TEAM-01..14); the 12 AI-native cells using the AI safety spec's titles; the trust boundary; the §12.6 rules mapped to AIS-*; a registry of every Plotinium ID prefix now in use; 39 prose obligations traced under the nearest ID; the ID grammar; the requirements.csv schema; the evidence path grammar (using the testing spec's project names); the gate-check algorithm; an errno coverage map; consolidated budgets; and TRC-01..08 tests.

All 24 Appendix B terms, each with the spec's meaning and how Plotinium realises it. About 150 Plotinium terms are grouped by subsystem: threads and kernel (executor, run token, special workers, blkio, kernel fencing epoch, kernel-link router, control block, watchdog, declared bound W with symbols matching the kernel spec, 5450 ms), memory (reservation-based admission, 85% watermark, speculative page, write-behind swap, codec), VFS, sync (op and control lanes, cseq, Lamport, credit window, owner feed, fencing token, os_session vs auth_session), server and database (vfsTxn, lockPlan, L0–L4, fault harness), boot (desktop-interactive, warm vs cold), WM, shell, AI (readable set, datamarking, intent binding, plan fingerprint with EAGAIN stale-plan, confirmation token with ENOTTY, cassette, time-bucketed MFU cold start), security, and delivery. It adds a disambiguation table for overloaded words (session, epoch/fence/version, lock, transaction, freeze, and others), a retired-terms table (HLC, ESTALE, per-uid IndexedDB, refresh+1 ms, Kernium, and others), and GLO-01..05. GLO-05 only warns on retired terms in docs and fails only on retired code identifiers, because negated mentions such as 'Lamport, not HLC' are legitimate.

Scheduling reply to the user's 'how long does it take?': the spec's plan is fixed at 18 weeks in five gated phases (registration W2, architecture defence W4, v0.2.0 W7, v0.3.0 W11, v0.4.0 W14, feature freeze W16, final defence and deployment W17–18). Production deployment is itself a Phase 2 deliverable (public URL at W7) and a final deliverable (§17.2), so deployment starts early rather than at the end.
